site_name: שכם (Shechem, Roman mausoleum)
author: I. el-Fani (staff officer's team)
location_note: In Shechem (Nablus), some distance east of Tell Balata (the quarter name is garbled in the text layer); no map reference.
notes: Found in a water-pipe trench; ornate facade with two groups of columns, door closed by a dressed stone door; frieze and pediment fragments.

site_name: סקר באתר ליד אל-בירה (survey of a site near el-Bira)
author: R. Blizzard (University of Texas at Austin)
location_note: Printed as '( 1451 1716 )' in the text layer; read as OIG E 1716 / N 1451 (INFERENCE: order reversed, as for el-Bira in the Ramallah district named in the text; the other order falls near Rosh ha-Ayin).
notes: Previously unknown site; 7,360 sq m surveyed (about half the site). Iron Age pottery from the 12th-11th centuries BCE, a little Hellenistic, mostly Roman and Byzantine. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ירושלים: הכנסייה הגרמנית במוריסטאן (Jerusalem, German church in the Muristan)
author: U. Lux (German Evangelical Institute)
location_note: Church of the Redeemer, Muristan; no map reference.
notes: Wall found in 1893 re-examined: south face exposed for 16.50 m; test pit to bedrock 13 m below the church floor; horizontal layers of the second half of the 1st century BCE, sloping fills tied to Agrippa II's expansion; the wall cannot be earlier than Agrippa II and is not the Second Wall (excavator's conclusion).

site_name: ירושלים: גבעת המבתר (Jerusalem, Giv'at ha-Mivtar, two burial caves)
author: D. Bahat; A. Kloner
location_note: Giv'at ha-Mivtar; no map references.
notes: Bahat's cave beside the cave dug the year before (ossuary inscribed 'Yezon'); Kloner's cave with eleven ossuaries, names 'Avshalom' and 'Qarya'.

site_name: ירושלים: הר הצופים - גן שולמית (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, Gan Shulamit, burial caves)
author: F. Vitto
location_note: Gan Shulamit, Mount Scopus; no map reference.
notes: First cave: square chamber with pit, four kokhim, three plain ossuaries, one inscribed 'Marta' in Aramaic. Two more caves dug in January 1972: one with two rooms and an ossuary inscribed 'Hananya and his son'; the second partly garbled in the text layer (two levels of kokhim; robbed).

site_name: ירושלים: הר הצופים - הגן הבוטני (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, botanical garden, burial caves)
author: (names garbled in the text layer; Hebrew University and Department of Antiquities)
location_note: Botanical garden of the Hebrew University on Mount Scopus; distance clause partly garbled. No map reference.
notes: The text layer of this page is heavily garbled (OCR); the number of caves and several names are unreadable and are not guessed. Readable: Jewish burial caves of the Second Temple period of the usual Jerusalem type (square chamber, central pit, kokhim), nine stone ossuaries with lids, Greek and Hebrew names; one cave collapsed; an old ammunition dump in one kokh removed by the army and police.

site_name: ירושלים: קרית משה (Jerusalem, Qiryat Moshe, burial cave)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Sirkis Street on the Qiryat Moshe - Giv'at Shaul boundary; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: קברים ליד "קברי המלכים" (Jerusalem, tombs near the 'Tombs of the Kings')
author: F. Vitto (supervision A. Kloner)
location_note: Salah ed-Din Street, East Jerusalem, part of a cemetery dug in the 1930s; no map reference.

site_name: אבו ע'וש - 1971 (Abu Ghosh, Neolithic site, fourth season)
author: M. Lechevallier (French Centre for Prehistoric Research, J. Perrot)
location_note: Neolithic site at Abu Ghosh; no map reference.
notes: Abu Ghosh (spelling variant; exploratory by-eye match, as in HA 24).

site_name: בית הכנסת העתיק בעין-גדי - 1971 (the ancient synagogue at En Gedi, 1971)
author: D. Barag and Y. Porath
location_note: En Gedi oasis; no map reference.
notes: Late synagogue (about the 5th century CE) with bema, Torah shrine phases (earliest probably 3rd century CE), fifth inscription; laver in the entrance corridor; houses and lanes of the Jewish town burnt in the Byzantine period. Under the early white mosaic, two strata of the end of the Second Temple period. The stepped plastered pool is coded ritual_bath under the stepped-pool rule (class INFERENCE; the report gives no function).

site_name: קברים מימי בית שני בעין גדי (Second Temple tombs at En Gedi)
author: D. Barag and Y. Porath (synagogue expedition)
location_note: Eastern foot of the spur of the En Gedi field school, by the Ein Feshkha - En Gedi road; no map reference.
notes: Tomb damaged by road works. Second tomb with a low stone enclosure and stepped benches (compared with Beth Shearim catacombs 14 and 20).; Sub-heading inside the En Gedi synagogue item; not in the portal table of contents.

site_name: שכם - 1972 (Shechem, Tell Balata)
author: W. G. Dever (Albright Institute)
location_note: Tell Balata; no map reference.
notes: Cyclopean wall A (MB IIC) re-exposed for about 85 m; 12-room building by the north-west gate dated about 1600 BCE. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: מאוזוליאום בשכם (ח' עסכר) (mausoleum in Shechem, Kh. Askar)
author: I. el-Fani (supervision Z. Yeivin)
location_note: Kh. Askar in Shechem, south-east slope of Mount Ebal; second tomb north of Askar. No map reference.
notes: Same mausoleum as HA41-017. Burial hall 5 x 5 m with three arcosolia and ten sarcophagi, Greek inscriptions (Iustus son of Iustus son of Theophilus, Archelais daughter of Simon son of Alexander; Sabbatius); attributed to a wealthy Samaritan family. A narrow opening in the east arcosolium leads to an unexcavated rock-cut cell. A cistern 'probably' in front of the facade is inferred by the report, not observed; not coded.

site_name: ח' רדנה - 1972 (Kh. Radana, 1972)
author: J. A. Callaway (with R. A. Cooley)
location_note: Kh. Radana (Ramallah); no map reference.
notes: Iron Age I village (founded about 1220, destroyed about 1050 BCE by the excavator); three houses round a common courtyard with stone pillars; copper and iron working; proto-Canaanite inscribed handle found in 1970; some Byzantine activity without houses.; The heading reads 'בח' רדנה (רמאללה)': Ramallah is a Z4 gazetteer name.

site_name: ירושלים: ככר צה"ל (Jerusalem, Kikar Tzahal)
author: M. Ben-Ari and D. Bahat
location_note: Kikar Tzahal outside the north-west corner of the Old City; no map reference.
notes: 'Goliath's Tower' (Tancred's Tower) shown to be Crusader, probably 12th century CE, not Psephinus; Crusader city wall about 2 m thick with a rock-cut moat about 18 m wide (fortification, not coded). The excavators identify Robinson's 'Third Wall' line here with the moat and the channel retaining wall.

site_name: ירושלים: גבעת המבתר (Jerusalem, Giv'at ha-Mivtar, completion of the Midbar Sinai Street cave)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Midbar Sinai Street, Giv'at ha-Mivtar; no map reference.
notes: Same cave as HA41-020 (Kloner's cave, dated there). Four northern kokhim cleared: five decorated ossuaries; inscriptions 'Shimon' (erased), 'Marya' or 'Qarya', and letters 'of the house of David'.

site_name: ירושלים: שועפט (Jerusalem, Shu'fat, shaft grave)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Northern edge of Shu'fat village. Printed as '(נ"צ 1357 1715)' in the text layer; read as OIG E 1715 / N 1357 (INFERENCE: order reversed in extraction or print).

site_name: ירושלים: קברים ליד "קברי המלכים" (Jerusalem, tombs near the 'Tombs of the Kings')
author: F. Vitto
location_note: Nablus Road corner of Salah ed-Din Street; no map reference.

site_name: מערת חריתון (Mearat Khareitun)
author: G. Man (student volunteers); pottery checked by A. Kloner
location_note: Wadi Khareitun south-east of Herodium; no map reference.
notes: Over 900 working hours; plan reaches more than 400 m from the entrance. Earlier surveys: Survey of Western Palestine and 1965.; Khareitun in the gazetteer (Z3). Not in a held cave area (plan section 7).

site_name: אזור פצאל (Fasael area)
author: Y. Porath
location_note: East of the Jericho - Beth Shean road, at the outlet of Nahal Fasael; several map references printed with the northing first in the text layer (e.g. '1615 1915' for the Chalcolithic building), read as E/N: Chalcolithic building 1915/1615, Israelite building 1924/1582, road points 1908-1922/1608-1617, longest qanat line from 19275/16195 to 19295/15980, Kh. ed-Dasha 1950/1587 (all in Z2).
notes: Chalcolithic (Ghassulian) house 16 x 17 m; Iron II building of the 8th century BCE; ancient road down from the Samaria hills (Byzantine sherds); terraces and clearance heaps undated. The report suggests from Josephus that Herod (Phasaelis) first led the spring water by aqueduct, but says the parts cannot be dated without test excavations. Umayyad farm of about 2,500 dunams with three main aqueducts of U-shaped stone segments (about 4 km), secondary channels with outlets every 7.5 m, bridges over the qanat channel; qanats (chain wells) dug after the farm system; coins after 712 CE.

site_name: ירושלים: החומה השלישית (Jerusalem, the Third Wall)
author: S. Ben-Arieh and E. Netzer (with Y. Levi)
location_note: Wall segment by the Nablus Road (area dug in 1926 by Sukenik and Mayer); no map reference.
notes: Wall 4.25 m wide exposed for 45 m, tower foundation 11 x 9 m; a plastered room built against the wall with 1st-century CE pottery: the excavators date the wall to the end of the Second Temple period (Third Wall). Fill of quarry waste under a lime floor. Byzantine public building above with a cross in relief and tabula ansata in a cistern wall.

site_name: ירושלים: הר ציון (Jerusalem, Mount Zion, mosaic floor at the American Institute)
author: A. Kloner (reported by J. Monson and B. Qupti)
location_note: Gobat school grounds, Mount Zion; no map reference.
notes: White mosaic of two rooms, 5th-6th-century pottery. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ירושלים: חומה חדשה ממערב לגן הארמני (Jerusalem, new wall west of the Armenian Garden)
author: M. Broshi (with N. Gershon)
location_note: About 100 m south of the Citadel, west of the Turkish city wall; no map reference.
notes: A further wall west of the Turkish wall (which stands on the Hasmonean First Wall), probably the Roman-Byzantine city wall. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ירושלים: מזרח תלפיות (Jerusalem, East Talpiyot, burial cave)
author: F. Vitto
location_note: Armon ha-Natziv area. Printed as '128700 172895' in the text layer; read as E 172895 / N 128700 (INFERENCE: northing first).

site_name: ירושלים: הגבעה הצרפתית (Jerusalem, French Hill, burial cave)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Gad young couples' housing, French Hill; no map reference.
notes: Eleven individuals (P. Smith).

site_name: ירושלים: עיסוויה (Jerusalem, ruin east of Isawiya)
author: A. Kloner and S. Gudovitch
location_note: About 1 km east of the centre of Isawiya. The map reference reads '1340 0848' in the text layer; it does not give a position near Isawiya in either order and is not used (garbled or misprinted).
notes: Ruin of about one dunam with walls of large stones and white mosaic floors; Byzantine sherds; probably a farm or monastery (surveyors' suggestion).

site_name: תל צופר (Tel Zofar, Tell Sufar, Shechem)
author: Z. Yeivin
location_note: Tell Sufar at the outlet of Nahal Shechem, western entrance of the city; no map reference.
notes: About 12 small test pits; six strata: Persian-Hellenistic granaries, late Iron Age walls, earlier buildings; layers 3-5 partly garbled in the text layer (one layer dated to the 9th century BCE). No feature of the eligible classes is described in the readable text.; Title not in the gazetteer; the text places it at the western entrance of Shechem (gazetteer name).

site_name: שכם (Shechem, mosaic)
author: (Israel Museum laboratories; text partly garbled)
location_note: Shechem; no map reference.
notes: The 2nd-century CE mosaic found half a year earlier was lifted; an earlier white mosaic with a black frame about 10 cm below. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ירושלים: הר הצופים (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, burial cave at the Supreme Court site)
author: V. Sussman and Y. Ziyyas
location_note: South-western foot of Mount Scopus, levelling for the Supreme Court building; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: עמק המצלבה (Jerusalem, Valley of the Cross, burial cave)
author: V. Sussman and Y. Ziyyas
location_note: Valley of the Cross (landscaping for the Jerusalem Foundation); no map reference.

site_name: תולילאת אבו אל-עלייק (Tulul Abu el-Alayiq, near Jericho)
author: E. Netzer (with Z. Yeivin)
location_note: North of Wadi Qelt near Jericho: northern tell (Kelso and Baramki's tell 2), the large pool east of it and the adjacent mound; no map reference.
notes: Mud-brick building under the building on the tell, with the frescoes Kelso and Baramki attributed to the upper building; ashlar wall 2.60 m thick. South of the pool foundations of a large building (20 x 17 m) later rebuilt; west of the pool a service building for bathers with a geometric mosaic. Pool function word reads 'שתייה' (drinking) in the text layer; the context (bathers) suggests 'שחייה' (swimming) but the word is not emended here.; Built-site excavation north of Wadi Qelt, not a cave report; read normally (plan section 7).

site_name: שכם - 1973 (Shechem, Tell Balata, north-west gate area)
author: W. G. Dever (Albright Institute)
location_note: North-west gate area of ancient Shechem (Tell Balata); no map reference.
notes: Building 7300 over Wall A (MB IIC), interpreted as a temple with a platform; casemate wall E; Iron Age sherds of the 10th-9th centuries BCE in two test pits. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: מוצא (Moza)
author: E. Eisenberg
location_note: By the Jerusalem - Tel Aviv road, south of the fort called Qasr el-Yahud (name partly garbled); no map reference.
notes: Crusader fort 30 x 15 m; Byzantine mosaics and ashlar walls; two Late Roman rooms burnt; two dwellings of the end of the Second Temple period with frescoes (prutah of Pontius Pilate, silver coin of Vespasian); Early Bronze apsidal buildings.

site_name: ירושלים: הרובע היהודי - 1973 (Jerusalem, Jewish Quarter, fifth season)
author: N. Avigad (with R. Reich, H. Geva, S. Margalit, N. Lapinsky, D. Castel, A. Pearl)
location_note: Nine areas in the Jewish Quarter (W, P, Q, Ts, R, T); no map references.
notes: Lowest stratum on rock of the Herodian period throughout; the descriptions refer mainly to it; all buildings burnt and destroyed at one time (area P1 room with stone vessels and coins of the Revolt; destroyed in 70 CE). Byzantine building in area T1 and wall in area R not eligible.

site_name: ירושלים: גבעת המבתר (Jerusalem, Giv'at ha-Mivtar, Mitzrei Tiran Street, burial cave)
author: R. Peled and O. Hess
location_note: Mitzrei Tiran Street, Giv'at ha-Mivtar; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: הר הצופים (הגן הבוטני) (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, botanical garden, tomb)
author: L. Y. Rahmani
location_note: Botanical garden, Mount Scopus; no map reference.
notes: Nine ossuaries, one inscribed 'Eliezer bar Zekharya'; iron ring with a red glass seal showing Fortuna; earliest burial with pottery earlier than the Herodian period; Herodian lamp.

site_name: ירושלים: קרית משה (Jerusalem, Qiryat Moshe, burial cave)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Kurot ha-Ittim Street opposite the Merkaz ha-Rav yeshiva, about 100 m west of the cave in HA41-023; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: בריכת הסולטן (Jerusalem, the Sultan's Pool)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Sultan's Pool, west of the Old City; no map reference.
notes: Section on the north side re-exposed the closing wall recorded by C. Schick. The channel at the bottom predates the reservoir (it drained the area before the pool was installed, below the base of the southern dam); its vault, of poured fieldstones, is not earlier than the Roman period and probably later. The dam itself was not excavated.

site_name: הרודיון - 1973 (Herodium, 1973)
author: E. Netzer (with E. Damati and S. Arzi)
location_note: Lower Herodium, north of the Beit Sahur - Tekoa road; foot of the mountain; no map reference.
notes: At least 20-30 dunams of Herodian palace and service buildings; Byzantine church of St Michael over them; ashlar building with a colonnaded hall reused in the Byzantine period; storehouse destroyed by an earthquake at the end of the Second Temple period, finally in the First Revolt.

site_name: אזור פצאל (Fasael area, enclosure north of Nahal Fasael)
author: (staff officer for archaeology team, with Y. Porath)
location_note: North of the Nahal Fasael stream bed; map reference printed '1914/1623' (E/N order as printed; 32.05 N 35.44 E).
notes: Large enclosure: square courtyard about 120 m a side and a walled built area 111 x 40 m with a central building; one occupation layer; 1st-century BCE pottery and a coin of Jannaeus. The excavators suggest a Hasmonean farm abandoned after a short time, replaced by Herod's Phasaelis to the south. No aqueduct seen between the Fasael springs and the enclosure.

site_name: יריחו: תולול אבו אל-עלייק (Jericho, Tulul Abu el-Alayiq)
author: E. Netzer (with A. Lass)
location_note: Both banks of Wadi Qelt at its outlet: north wing opposite the sunken garden and the south tell (Kelso and Baramki's tell 1), the north tell (tell 2); a round tower about 1 km west of the north tell at the ascent of Tariq el-Hindi; no map reference.
notes: North wing of Herod's winter palace: reception hall 29 x 19 m, two courts, bathhouse with round frigidarium, opus reticulatum and quadratum; parts still in use at the end of the Second Temple period; a 2nd-century CE building burnt; last occupation end of the Byzantine period. North tell: late Hasmonean palace (central building about 65 x 50 m) with the plastered surrounds of the large swimming pool (HA47-018), which the excavator links with Josephus' account of the drowning of Aristobulus III; the surrounds went out of use when the Herodian artificial mound and garden covered them. Round tower 10.8 m in diameter probably of the end of the Second Temple period. The coin hoard is probably the one reported in HA 47 (same count and ruler).; Built-site excavation at the outlet of Wadi Qelt, not a cave report; read normally (plan section 7).

site_name: ירושלים: אבו תור - ה'תיאטרון' (Jerusalem, Abu Tor, Schick's 'theatre')
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Eastern end of Abu Tor, about 550 m from the south-east corner of the Second Temple city wall, south of Siloam; no map reference.
notes: Schick's proposed theatre (Josephus, Antiquities 15) not confirmed; few Roman and Byzantine sherds, more later sherds. PDF pages 16 and 17 carry the same printed page (15) twice; the span uses the first copy.

site_name: ירושלים: גבעת מרדכי (Jerusalem, Giv'at Mordechai, burial cave)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Shahal Street, Giv'at Mordechai, opposite nos. 19-20; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: אמת המים 'הנמוכה' (Jerusalem, the low-level aqueduct, conservation)
author: A. Lass
location_note: Between Armon ha-Natziv and Abu Tor, below the St Clare convent; tunnel at Armon ha-Natziv; East Talpiyot; no map reference.
notes: Conservation and a check of the blockage in the Armon ha-Natziv tunnel; earlier survey by A. Mazar and Y. Cohen (HA31-019).

site_name: חדשות בקצרה: העופל (brief news: the Ophel, Jerusalem, conservation)
author: (Department of Antiquities; L. Wolt)
location_note: Kenyon's excavations on the Ophel; no map reference.
notes: Conservation of late First Temple period buildings and of the glacis Kenyon dated to MB II. No feature of the eligible classes.; Sub-item of the brief news item; Ophel is in Jerusalem.

site_name: אבו ע'וש (Abu Ghosh, rock-cut tomb)
author: G. Ziyas (Department of Antiquities)
location_note: Abu Ghosh village (house foundations); no map reference.
notes: Abu Ghosh (spelling variant; exploratory by-eye match, as in HA 24).

site_name: בית זית (Beit Zayit)
author: E. Eisenberg
location_note: Beit Zayit, foundations for the extension of the village shop; no map reference.
notes: Byzantine wall remains above. The pool and channel are called an agricultural or industrial installation by the report.

site_name: ירושלים: הר הצופים (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, burial caves on the south slope)
author: A. Kloner (with E. Netzer and Y. Ziyas)
location_note: South slope of the Mount Scopus campus facing the Old City; no map reference.
notes: About 35 ossuaries; names Hananya (Greek), Yehuda, Elazar, Hananya son of Shimon; a large limestone coffin-ossuary inscribed 'of Phasael' and later 'of Phasael his son and of Iphigenia'. Site released for building.

site_name: ירושלים: הגבעה הצרפתית (Jerusalem, French Hill, burial cave)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: East of French Hill above the Kamdav housing (planned WIZO home); no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: גת שמנים (Jerusalem, Gethsemane)
author: C. Spiro (with C. Katsimbinis)
location_note: Temporary cemetery of the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate at Gethsemane, by the Armenian cemetery dug in 1936; no map reference.
notes: Crusader mosaic of a church (basilica) and its forecourt; monastery attested from the Byzantine period to Saladin; Byzantine remains seen but not excavated.

site_name: ירושלים: הר ציון - ביצורים מימי הבית השני (Jerusalem, Mount Zion, Second Temple fortifications)
author: M. Broshi (with N. Gershon, S. Eldar, J. Sasson)
location_note: Foot of the western city wall between the Citadel and the south-west corner of the Old City (about 275 m); no map reference.
notes: Hasmonean (First) wall under the Turkish wall for at least 115 m, four towers; a forewall attributed probably to Herod. Walls and towers not eligible.

site_name: ירושלים: הר הזיתים (Jerusalem, Mount of Olives, painted burial cave)
author: A. Kloner (with G. Ziyas)
location_note: West slope of the Mount of Olives, south-west of the Commodore hotel (es-Suwwana area); no map reference.
notes: Painted cave: vines, birds and a peacock on walls and ceiling; two letters of a Greek inscription. The older cave was broken into from the painted one.

site_name: ירושלים: הר ציון - מגדל שער מימי הביניים (Jerusalem, Mount Zion, medieval gate tower)
author: M. Broshi (with P. Burke, N. Gershon, Y. Eldar, J. Sasson)
location_note: About 100 m east of Zion Gate, opposite Habad and Jews' Streets; no map reference.
notes: Ayyubid gate tower of 1212 with a monumental Arabic inscription. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ירושלים: הר הצופים (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, humanities building site)
author: A. Kloner and Y. Gat
location_note: Hebrew University humanities building site, Mount Scopus, near the cave of HA51-024; no map reference.
notes: The excavators call the stepped installation a cistern ('בור מים'); it is coded ritual_bath under the stepped-pool rule with that label kept (class INFERENCE).

site_name: ירושלים: מערות קבורה מתקופת הברזל (Jerusalem, Iron Age burial caves north of the Damascus Gate)
author: A. Kloner and G. Barkay; A. Mazar (identification of the 1937 caves)
location_note: Rocky hill between Nablus Road and Salah ed-Din Street: St Etienne (Dominican) monastery grounds and the Garden Tomb; two caves found in 1937 north of the Damascus Gate; no map references.
notes: Caves with benches, head-rests and repositories, without kokhim or arcosolia; Byzantine reuse (painted crosses); lamps of the 7th century BCE in the Garden Tomb collection.

site_name: ירושלים: דרך חברון (Jerusalem, Hebron Road, burial caves)
author: D. Davis and A. Kloner
location_note: Hebron Road between the foot of Mount Zion and the Sultan's Pool; no map reference.
notes: Sealed fourth cave: two rooms with benches and a bone repository, about 20 individuals, seal of Hanni'el (or Hamiel) daughter of Menahem; 7th century BCE.

site_name: ירושלים: מערת האשכולות (Jerusalem, the Cave of the Grapes, cleaning)
author: A. Kloner (supervision)
location_note: Public garden in Ramot Eshkol; no map reference.
notes: Same cave as HA28-028 (HA 28-29). Courtyard 7.3 x 6.8 m and entrance room cleared; burial rooms not cleaned; sherds from the fill medieval and Ottoman.

site_name: ירושלים: הרובע היהודי - 1974 (Jerusalem, Jewish Quarter, sixth season)
author: N. Avigad (with R. Reich, H. Geva, S. Margalit, Z. Maoz, A. Pearl)
location_note: Mainly the Yeshivat ha-Kotel site (areas W and P), a strip about 110 m long; areas A5 and T1 outside it; no map references.
notes: Main remains in the stratum attributed to the time of Herod, mostly on rock: a mansion of about 600 sq m overlooking the Temple Mount (areas P and W2) burnt in the Roman destruction; area P3 another large building; stone table, coins of the Revolt. Area A5: the Israelite city wall traced 6 m further. Area T1: large Byzantine building (perhaps the Nea), Herodian stratum reached in two squares.

site_name: ירושלים: חפירה ליד שער האשפות (Jerusalem, excavation by the Dung Gate)
author: M. Ben-Dov (Temple Mount excavations, B. Mazar)
location_note: West of the Dung Gate outside the city wall, at the outlet of the Gallicantu road; no map reference.
notes: Turkish wall on an Umayyad wall; Ayyubid tower perhaps on Crusader fortifications; paved street (or square) over 17 m wide and 60 m long leading from the Western Wall area to Mount Zion, in use in Aelia Capitolina; ashlar structures (tower?) under it tied to the large rock-cut cavity; Byzantine and Muslim or Crusader buildings.

site_name: ירושלים: הר הצופים (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, two burial caves)
author: A. Kloner (with Y. Gat, A. Lass, A. de Groot, E. Braun)
location_note: (a) East slope of Mount Scopus (Readymix plant); (b) between the education and humanities buildings of the Hebrew University; no map references.
notes: Cave (b): eighteen ossuaries, many decorated and inscribed ('Yirut daughter of Nadav', 'Pinhas son of Yosef', 'tomb of Ami').

site_name: ירושלים: הגבעה הצרפתית (Jerusalem, French Hill, two burial caves with a common courtyard)
author: A. Kloner (with Y. Gat); G. Ziyas (east cave)
location_note: French Hill development area; no map reference.
notes: West cave: seven ossuaries, a Greek inscription naming Mattiah and Shim'on his brother, 'Mariame wife of Mattia' with a curse, other names. East cave: square room with three kokhim, empty.

site_name: ירושלים: רמות אשכול (Jerusalem, Ramot Eshkol, burial caves)
author: A. Kloner (with Y. Votkin)
location_note: Ramat ha-Golan Street, Ramot Eshkol, near the Cave of the Grapes; no map reference.
notes: Robbed; two smashed ossuaries, one inscribed 'Markios' twice in Greek; a second cave nearby found empty (not coded separately). Northern continuation of the Sanhedriya cave group.

site_name: יריחו - תולול אבו אל-עלייק (Jericho, Tulul Abu el-Alayiq, 1975)
author: E. Netzer (with A. Lass, D. Stacey, G. Kopel)
location_note: Hasmonean palace complex north of Wadi Qelt; aqueducts west and north of the site; no map reference.
notes: Plastered surround west of the swimming pool with Herodian flowerpots; a building area with three Hasmonean strata and a Herodian one; Hasmonean bathhouse with the earliest mosaic known in the country; a 2nd-century CE house over the Herodian palace, burnt probably in the Bar Kokhba revolt; boundary walls of royal estates attributed to the Hasmonean period. The excavator calls part or most of the pools miqvaot.; Built-site excavation at the outlet of Wadi Qelt, not a cave report; read normally (plan section 7).

site_name: ירושלים: ארמון הנציב (Jerusalem, Armon ha-Natziv, burial cave)
author: Y. Gat
location_note: Armon ha-Natziv building area; no map reference.

site_name: יריחו - תל א-סמראת (Jericho, Tell es-Samarat)
author: E. Netzer
location_note: Tell es-Samarat south of Tell Jericho; no map reference.
notes: Artificial mound probably built by Herod: large building about 70 x 55 m with a semicircular stepped structure (radius about 35 m); hippodrome about 320 x 80 m to the south, identified by the excavator with Josephus' hippodrome. No feature of the eligible classes.; Tell es-Samarat (spelling variant), south of ancient Jericho.

site_name: קיפרוס (תל אל-עקבה) (Kypros, Tell el-Aqaba)
author: E. Netzer and E. Damati
location_note: South of the outlet of Wadi Qelt. Printed '1392 / 1903'; read as OIG E 1903 / N 1392 (INFERENCE: northing first, as elsewhere in these volumes; the other order falls on the coastal plain).
notes: Hasmonean remains on the summit (outer wall, rooms) and a round tower on the lower terrace; Herodian fortress-palace on the summit and lower terrace, identified with Kypros (Josephus); burning attributed to the First Revolt; a small Byzantine monastery (?) with a chapel.; Built-site excavation south of the outlet of Wadi Qelt, not a cave report; read normally (plan section 7).

site_name: הרודיון - 1974 (Herodium, cisterns and tunnels)
author: E. Netzer and S. Arzi
location_note: Inside the mountain of Herodium and the east part of its courtyard; no map reference.
notes: The Herodian cistern system went out of use when the tunnels were cut; a narrow, mostly destroyed tunnel perhaps of the First Revolt. Kiln of the First Revolt; dozens of coins, mostly of the First Revolt and some of the Second; arrowheads; Hebrew ostracon.

site_name: רוג'ם אבו מוח'ייר (Rujm Abu Muhayir)
author: Z. Yeivin (with I. el-Fani and D. Bakar)
location_note: On the road west from Fasael, at the pass between the Jordan Valley and the hills; no map reference.
notes: Round building of three concentric rings, 19.40 m across, with radial rooms; large pithos sherds probably of the end of the Iron Age. No feature of the eligible classes.; Not in the gazetteer; the text places it on the road leading west from Fasael (gazetteer name) at the pass between the Jordan Valley and the hills. INFERENCE: at about the western edge of the Z2 box.

site_name: ירושלים: הגבעה הצרפתית (Jerusalem, French Hill, three burial caves)
author: A. Kloner and R. Sivan
location_note: East slope of French Hill, edge of the WIZO day-care plot (near HA51-025); no map reference.
notes: Third cave: crosses incised on the wall and on lamps; Christian burials, perhaps of the Byzantine farm or a nearby monastery.

site_name: ירושלים: מנחת (Jerusalem, Manahat, rock-cut tomb with a lead coffin)
author: Y. Gat
location_note: Manahat, shelter foundations; no map reference.
notes: Decorated lead coffin with cupids; two men; gold earrings, gold and glass beads, gold ring with an engraved shrimp, gold threads.

site_name: חדשות בקצרה: דיר אל-חטב (brief news: Deir el-Hatab near Shechem, rock-cut caves)
author: I. el-Fani (staff officer for archaeology team)
location_note: Hill south-east of the village of Deir el-Hatab near Shechem; no map reference.
notes: Three rock-cut caves exposed after robbing.; Sub-item of the brief news; the text places Deir el-Hatab near Shechem (gazetteer name).

site_name: חדשות בקצרה: רוג'ייב (brief news: Rujeib south-east of Shechem, burial cave)
author: I. el-Fani
location_note: Rujeib, south-east of Shechem; no map reference.
notes: Sub-item of the brief news; the text places Rujeib south-east of Shechem (gazetteer name).

site_name: חדשות בקצרה: עין סמיה (brief news: Ein Samiya, salvage excavation by a new road)
author: W. Zeidan (Ramallah district inspector)
location_note: By the ancient cemetery of Ein Samiya, on both sides of the wadi; no map reference.
notes: Sub-item of the brief news. The text layer reads 'עין ממיה'; read as Ein Samiya (INFERENCE: the ס/מ confusion is systematic in this text layer; Ramallah district, by the ancient cemetery).

site_name: ח' מרג'מה (עין סמיה) (Kh. Marjama, Ein Samiya)
author: A. Mazar (with A. Barhum and S. Yankelevitch)
location_note: Hill at the end of a long spur above Ein Samiya; settlement of about 40 dunams; no map reference.
notes: Iron Age II fortified town (tower on a podium, wall 4 m wide plus retaining walls), houses with 9th-8th century BCE pottery; bronze bowl. Earlier suggestion of a cult place on the cupmarked rock surface (not tested by the report). Identification proposals: Ephraim (Albright), Baal-shalishah (Kallai).

site_name: ירושלים: חפירות ליד חומת העיר המערבית (Jerusalem, excavations by the western city wall)
author: M. Broshi (with N. Gershon, an assistant named Eliot (surname not given), S. Gibson, J. Sasson)
location_note: About 280 m along the western wall between the Citadel and the south-west corner; no map reference.
notes: Hasmonean wall under the Turkish wall for about 120 m, an earlier tower; Herodian forewall with two towers; Aelia Capitolina wall segments; Ayyubid inscription of al-Mu'azzam Isa of 1202 and demolition debris. Walls not eligible.

site_name: ירושלים: הר הצופים (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, botanical garden, two burial caves)
author: Y. Gat; A. Kloner and Y. Gat (with D. Melamed)
location_note: Botanical garden on Mount Scopus and its north slope; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: העופל (Jerusalem, the Ophel, Ir David road)
author: Y. Gat (with A. Abu Khalil)
location_note: Ir David road (Wadi Tilweh), Ophel; no map reference.
notes: Wall segments marked by Bliss; perhaps fortifications of the western hill in the Second Temple period; First and Second Temple sherds. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ירושלים: אזור הכנסייה הסקוטית (Jerusalem, area of the Scottish church)
author: G. Barkay (with D. Hamilton and A. Abu Khalil)
location_note: Small hill between the road to Mount Zion and the road up to the Scottish church, near the railway station; no map reference.
notes: Large threshold in situ; opus sectile and gilded glass wall-mosaic tesserae of a Byzantine church; Iron Age sherds (8th-7th centuries BCE) without structures. A built, vaulted underground ashlar room south of the graves (entered through a shaft) is a built structure, not coded.

site_name: ירושלים: בית וגן (Jerusalem, Bayit va-Gan, burial cave)
author: A. Kloner and D. Davis
location_note: Girls' school building site, Bayit va-Gan; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: מערת האשכולות (Jerusalem, the Cave of the Grapes, cleaning continued)
author: (Department of Antiquities staff)
location_note: Ramot Eshkol; no map reference.
notes: Same cave as HA28-028 and HA53-023. Ornamented facade; ossuaries smashed during the later use; many animal bones; hard packed fill; plan drawn by Macalister in 1900.

site_name: ירושלים: אוגוסטה ויקטוריה (Jerusalem, Augusta Victoria, burial cave)
author: Y. Gat (with D. Melamed and D. Stacey)
location_note: East slope of the hill of the Augusta Victoria hospital (a-Tur); no map reference.
notes: Two sarcophagi and a large ossuary in an antiquities shop were probably robbed from this cave.

site_name: ירושלים: כיכר צה"ל (Jerusalem, Kikar Tzahal, Fast hotel site)
author: D. Davis
location_note: Site of the former Fast hotel; no map reference.
notes: Dump soil with First Temple to medieval sherds; 4th-century CE sherds on the rock; Turkish guard house. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ירושלים: מזרח תלפיות (Jerusalem, East Talpiyot, burial cave)
author: Y. Gat (with D. Stacey, I. Votkin, D. Melamed)
location_note: East Talpiyot (Armon ha-Natziv) building area; no map reference.

site_name: נתיב הגדוד (Netiv HaGedud)
author: O. Bar-Yosef (site found by Z. Shavit)
location_note: Lower Jordan Valley at Netiv HaGedud; no map reference.
notes: Pre-Pottery Neolithic site of about 10 dunams; round structures, flint and stone tools; loose flat stone blocks with cupmarks (not rock-cut). No feature of the eligible classes. The end of the item is not continued on the next PDF page (layout).

site_name: בית נקופה (Beit Neqofa, tomb)
author: O. Hess
location_note: West foot of a hill at Beit Neqofa; no map reference.
notes: Beit Neqofa (by-eye match; west of Jerusalem inside the Z4 box).

site_name: ירושלים: כנסייה צלבנית (Jerusalem, a Crusader church in Ma'alot ha-Midrasha Street)
author: (Department of Antiquities)
location_note: Ma'alot ha-Midrasha Street ('Aqabat Khalidiya), Old City; no map reference.
notes: Crusader church preserved inside a workshop, perhaps St Julian. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ירושלים: רחוב שמעון הצדיק (Jerusalem, Shim'on ha-Tzaddiq Street, burial cave)
author: A. Kloner and Y. Gat
location_note: By the Ma'alot Dafna kindergarten; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: גן הפעמון (Jerusalem, Liberty Bell Garden)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Between King David Street and Bloomfield Garden and Yitzhak Elhanan Street; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: קרית יובל - מנחת (Jerusalem, site south of Qiryat Yovel)
author: S. Gibson and G. Barkay
location_note: Spur at the junction of Nahal Refaim and Nahal Manahat (Ras ...), opposite Ein Yalo; map reference 1671/1282 as printed.
notes: At least three buildings with monolithic pillars, a long massive wall, Arab field tower; Iron Age (lmlk impression) and Persian sherds.

site_name: ירושלים: כביש ירושלים - רמאללה (Jerusalem, Jerusalem - Ramallah road, winepress)
author: A. Kloner and Y. Gat
location_note: Junction of the Ramallah road with the Anata road; map reference 17223/13508 as printed.

site_name: ירושלים: רחבת שער שכם (Jerusalem, Damascus Gate plaza, vaults)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Plaza inside the Damascus Gate; no map reference.
notes: Vaults supporting the present plaza, contemporary with the present gate threshold; Byzantine plaza level below (Madaba map).

site_name: ירושלים: שיח' ג'רח - אתר פריהיסטורי (Jerusalem, Sheikh Jarrah, prehistoric site)
author: D. Davis
location_note: East of the national police headquarters, Sheikh Jarrah; no map reference.
notes: Acheulean-like flint industry in clay layers. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ירושלים: רחוב הנוצרים (Jerusalem, Christian Quarter Street)
author: S. Margalit
location_note: Christian Quarter Street, Old City; no map reference.
notes: Street paved with large slabs, 60 cm below today's street; late Roman or early Byzantine sherds under the slabs; probably the Patriarch's street (Madaba map). No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ירושלים: כביש רמות - סנהדריה (Jerusalem, Ramot - Sanhedriya road, kokhim cave)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Ramot - Sanhedriya road works; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: רחוב הגיא (Jerusalem, HaGai Street)
author: O. Hess and E. Eisenberg (supervision)
location_note: HaGai Street between the Chain Street and the Cotton Market; no map reference.
notes: Diagonal-paved street about 4 m below the present level, Roman sherds below it; the Tyropoeon street of the Madaba map. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ירושלים: כפר שאול (Jerusalem, Kfar Shaul, rock-cut tomb)
author: E. Eisenberg
location_note: Industrial zone by Kfar Shaul; no map reference.

site_name: תל א-סמראת (Tell es-Samarat, Jericho, second season)
author: E. Netzer
location_note: South of ancient Jericho; no map reference.
notes: Hippodrome 315 x 83 m, theatre-like semicircular structure 70 m across and a platform 70 x 70 m; attributed to Herod. No feature of the eligible classes.; Tell es-Samarat south of Tell Jericho (text); gazetteer name Jericho.

site_name: ירושלים: הר הצופים (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, botanical garden, burial cave)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Botanical garden, Mount Scopus; no map reference.

site_name: תולול אבו אל-עלייק - 1976/7 (Tulul Abu el-Alayiq, fifth season)
author: E. Netzer
location_note: South-east of the Hasmonean palace, by the large Herodian building; no map reference.
notes: A palace wing with residence, swimming pool, ornamental garden and bathhouse (called 'Roman' by the report), built over Hasmonean remains; Herodian service buildings and empty storerooms east of the Hasmonean swimming-pool complex.; Built-site excavation at the outlet of Wadi Qelt, not a cave report; read normally (plan section 7).

site_name: ח' מרג'מה (עין סמיה) (Kh. Marjama, Ein Samiya, 1978)
author: A. Mazar (with A. de Groot, B. Goz, D. Tarler, S. Yankelevitch)
location_note: Kh. Marjama by Ein Samiya; no map reference.
notes: Iron II wall and three rooms (8th century BCE destruction); the summit rock surface formerly thought a cult platform holds foundation cuttings of a massive building (35 x 15 m) with a rounded tower, not later than the 10th century BCE.; TOC title 'ח' מרדקמה' (portal spelling); heading 'מררמה (עין סמיה)' in the text layer; Kh. Marjama by Ein Samiya (gazetteer).

site_name: מבשרת ירושלים (Mevasseret Yerushalayim)
author: G. Edelstein and E. Eisenberg (survey by D. Davis)
location_note: End of a spur facing east to Moza and Nahal Soreq, at the yeshiva building site; a perennial spring above; no map reference.
notes: Agricultural terraces up to 5 m high with Iron Age sherds; Early Arab building; Byzantine and Second Temple occupation suggested; wall about 3 m wide with 8th-7th century BCE pottery; possible identification with biblical Moza (excavators).

site_name: ירושלים: הרובע היהודי 1976-1977 (Jerusalem, Jewish Quarter, eighth and ninth seasons)
author: N. Avigad (with H. Geva, R. Reich, S. Margalit, Z. Maoz, R. Rubin, H. Misgav)
location_note: Areas along the Jews' Street (cardo), by the Turkish city wall (areas T2, T4, 14, H3); no map references.
notes: Israelite 'broad wall' traced 65 m; Hasmonean First Wall segment; Byzantine cardo 22.5 m wide; Hasmonean and Herodian buildings (destroyed 70 CE) under a stepped Byzantine street; Crusader hall later a Mamluk workshop with water installations; Ayyubid tower of 1212. Area 14: vaulted substructure of the Nea church with Justinian's inscription (549/550 CE).

site_name: ירושלים: חפירות לאורך חומת העיר המערבית (Jerusalem, excavations along the western city wall, final)
author: M. Broshi (with G. Blumberg, E. Braun, N. Gershon, S. Gibson)
location_note: Between the Citadel and the south-west corner of the Old City, and south of the corner; no map reference.
notes: Hasmonean wall (probably John Hyrcanus I), Herodian additions and towers; Second Temple gate approach with stairs, breach probably by Titus repaired in the Roman period; Iron Age suburb buildings (7th century BCE); Ayyubid tower. Walls not eligible.

site_name: ירושלים: מבנה אופוס רטיקולטום (Jerusalem, the opus reticulatum building north-west of the Damascus Gate)
author: S. Ben-Arieh and E. Netzer
location_note: About 250 m north-west of the Damascus Gate, found by C. Schick in 1879; no map reference.
notes: Foundations of two concentric circles (33 m and 12 m across) with opus reticulatum like Herod's winter palace at Jericho; no sunken court. The excavators consider that it was a monument or mausoleum, perhaps the 'monument of the house of Herod' in Josephus; coded as a possible funerary monument (excavators' suggestion, not established). Byzantine pits.

site_name: ירושלים: עיר דוד (Jerusalem, City of David, by Birket el-Hamra)
author: Y. Shiloh (with G. Solar, A. de Groot; A. Kloner)
location_note: Southern edge of the City of David at Birket el-Hamra, mouth of the Tyropoeon at the Kidron; bulldozer trench east of the road; no map reference.
notes: Section through a wall 3.5 m wide (Bliss and Dickie's M2 scarp) and two further walls; a dump of complete and broken vessels (cooking pots, jars, Herodian lamp, stone vessels, glass) of the second half of the 1st century BCE to the early 1st century CE covering the third wall; the second and third walls predate it and probably stood before Herod. The report restates Bliss and Dickie's plan: two parallel wall lines closing the central valley, serving as fortification and as a dam for the pools. The pottery dump is a discard deposit, not a concealed cache; not coded.

site_name: ירושלים: רחוב מלכיצדק (Jerusalem, Malkizedek Street)
author: G. Edelstein
location_note: South of the Dung Gate, sewer trench by the paved street exposed by M. Ben-Dov; no map reference.
notes: Terraced building with mosaics (several plaster phases); a wall founded in a rock-cut trench at least 30 m long; 1st-century BCE sherds on the rock.

site_name: ירושלים: שכונת גילה (Jerusalem, Gilo, Iron Age site)
author: A. Mazar
location_note: West of the Gilo neighbourhood (site found by M. Kochavi in 1968); no map reference.
notes: Iron II tower, Arab reuse; Iron I unwalled settlement. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: תולול אבו אל-עלייק - 1978 (Tulul Abu el-Alayiq, sixth season)
author: E. Netzer (with R. Bar-Nathan, R. Birger, D. Stacey)
location_note: Hasmonean palace under the north mound; areas south of the swimming pool and about 250 m east of the Hasmonean palace; no map reference.
notes: North-west corner of the central building of the Hasmonean palace with stucco imitating marble; Hasmonean rooms near the large miqveh of the previous season; storehouse with liquid-storage jars in a craft area about 250 m east, near a pair of pools ('miqveh?') found earlier (not coded again).; Built-site excavation at the outlet of Wadi Qelt, not a cave report; read normally (plan section 7).

site_name: גלגל (Gilgal, Neolithic site)
author: T. Noy (with J. Schuldenrein)
location_note: Gilgal: spurs of the Lisan marl and a limestone ridge; no map reference.
notes: Pre-Pottery Neolithic A round structures, stone and basalt tools, a unique stone figurine, a late Natufian site nearby. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: אל-ירכה (ליד פצאל) (el-Yarka, near Fasael)
author: Y. Porath
location_note: East of the Fasael plain, against the enclosure wall of the Early Arab farm (HA46-009); no usable map reference.
notes: Building with a courtyard, kitchen and a mosaic-paved guest room with benches; Early Arab pottery (7th-8th centuries CE). No feature of the eligible classes.; Not in the gazetteer; the heading names Fasael (gazetteer name). The printed map reference is garbled in the text layer ('596 1933/1') and is not used.

site_name: ירושלים: עיר דוד - 1978 (Jerusalem, City of David, first season)
author: Y. Shiloh
location_note: Areas A, B, D, E, G on the eastern slope of the City of David (Rothschild land); no map references.
notes: Area A: two parallel walls above Birket el-Hamra; thousands of broken 1st-century CE vessels (not later than 70 CE) against the north wall; a corner (tower?) of the Iron Age below. Area D: wall of the First Wall line (about 18 m long, 3.5 m wide) with a small gate blocked probably on the eve of the Revolt. Area E: thick wall (or retaining wall) covered by the debris of 70 CE; four Iron II building phases. Area G: Hasmonean or Herodian glacis; first clear Persian layer. Finds include lmlk, Yehud and Rhodian stamps and a monumental Hebrew inscription fragment (late 8th century BCE).

site_name: ירושלים: רחוב הפלמ"ח (Jerusalem, Palmach Street, burial cave)
author: (Department of Antiquities staff)
location_note: Palmach Street 73; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: הר הזיתים (Jerusalem, Mount of Olives, shaft tomb)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: Lane from the Eleona church down towards Gethsemane; map reference 17309/13175 as printed.
notes: Roman and Byzantine sherds and mosaic tesserae in the sewer trench section.

site_name: ירושלים: אמת מים בהר ציון (Jerusalem, aqueduct on Mount Zion)
author: (Department of Antiquities supervision; Jerusalem Foundation)
location_note: About 50 m of the 'lower' aqueduct at the foot of the west slope of Mount Zion, the stretch round the Sultan's Pool; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: סביל בריכת הסולטאן (Jerusalem, the sabil by the Sultan's Pool)
author: (East Jerusalem Development Company; P. Bugod)
location_note: Sabil of Suleiman by the Sultan's Pool; no map reference.
notes: Original trough of the early Turkish period found 0.7 m below the newer one and restored. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: קלנדיה - חווה חקלאית (Qalandiya, agricultural farm)
author: Y. Magen
location_note: Qalandiya by the Atarot airfield; farm about 120 x 70 m, part of a large settlement; no map reference.
notes: Farm founded in the mid-3rd century BCE (Ptolemaic and Seleucid coins), developed until Agrippa I, still occupied at the end of the Second Temple period (coins of year 3, 68 CE, in the south building); north building Hellenistic core enlarged in the Hasmonean period; south building Hasmonean, later a stable, then fortified (scale armour like Masada's); 5th-6th-century CE coins and pottery on the surface. Many Second Temple tombs and winepresses known around Qalandiya.

site_name: ח'אן אל-אחמר (Khan el-Ahmar, monastery of St Euthymius)
author: Y. Meimaris
location_note: Monastery of St Euthymius at Khan el-Ahmar; no map reference.
notes: Main church floor cleared and repaired; vaulted crypt under the nave cleaned; refectory with six stone tables; storerooms destroyed in the earthquake of 659 CE; Umayyad and 12th-century finds.

site_name: הרודיון - 1978 (Lower Herodium, third season)
author: E. Netzer (with R. Bar-Nathan, R. Birger, D. Stacey)
location_note: Lower Herodium, west of the course; no map reference.
notes: Herodian ashlar hall (15 x 14 m) with niches, frescoed, reused in the Byzantine period; Herodian barrel-vaulted room; church of St Michael with baptistery and two Greek dedications.

site_name: ח' מרצץ (Kh. el-Murassas, monastery and orchards)
author: E. Damati
location_note: Map reference 178/133 as printed (OIG, 1 km precision).
notes: Large monastery (76 x 67 m) with a three-apsed church, mosaic-paved atrium, refectory with a marble table, annexes with a built manger; 6th-century CE Byzantine coins and lamps with crosses in a dump. Three terraced orchards with irrigation systems; the report does not date them separately.; Not in the gazetteer; zoned by its map reference (Z3).

site_name: מבשרת ירושלים (Mevasseret Yerushalayim, second season)
author: G. Edelstein (with H. Wikén and G. Ein Dor)
location_note: Mevasseret Yerushalayim; no map reference.
notes: Settlement of the Israelite (founded 8th-7th centuries BCE), Roman, Byzantine and Early Arab periods; wide wall perhaps a fortification; agricultural terraces up to 3 m high on the hills of Mevasseret Yerushalayim and Mevasseret Zion; study of the agricultural system with A. Horowitz and M. Kislev.

site_name: ירושלים: חפירות בין שער שכם לשער החדש (Jerusalem, excavations between the Damascus Gate and the New Gate)
author: D. Tarler, A. de Groot and G. Solar
location_note: Outside the northern Old City wall between the Damascus Gate and the New Gate; no map reference.
notes: Crusader wall and rock-cut moat (about 14 m wide); Byzantine wall line under the Turkish wall; no Iron Age or Second Temple sherds. Fortifications not eligible.

site_name: ירושלים: הר הצופים (Jerusalem, Mount Scopus, two burial caves facing Isawiya)
author: A. Kloner
location_note: North-east part of Mount Scopus opposite Isawiya; no map reference.

site_name: ירושלים: מאגר מים מקומר (Jerusalem, vaulted water reservoir on the Jerusalem - Ramallah road)
author: A. Kloner (with Y. Votkin)
excavated_or_surveyed: inspected (recorded); later destroyed by the contractor
location_note: Between French Hill (Giv'at Shapira) and Giv'at ha-Mivtar; map reference 17226/13439 as printed.
notes: Reservoir 8 x 4.2 m, about 5.5 m high, ashlar barrel vault of twenty courses with draw openings, built into a pit cut in flint breccia; several plaster phases. The report suggests a fort and the Scopus of Josephus at this lookout point (suggestion only). No sherds.

site_name: גבעון (Gibeon, shaft tombs)
author: D. Davis
location_note: Valley north-west of Gibeon; no map reference.
notes: Previously unknown MB I cemetery under silt; Roman road remains and three uninscribed milestones on the surface.; Gibeon (el-Jib) by eye, inside the Z4 box (as HA 31-32).

site_name: שכם (Shechem, Neapolis remains)
author: (staff officer for archaeology; I. el-Fani)
location_note: Arion quarter on the lower slope of Mount Gerizim; Amman Street at the foot of Mount Ebal; no map reference.
notes: Ashlar walls, cornices and arch stones attributed to the founding of Neapolis (second half of the 1st century CE); three Corinthian capitals. No feature of the eligible classes.

site_name: ואדי קלט (Wadi Qelt, water mill)
author: Y. Porath (aqueduct survey of the Jericho area)
location_note: About 20 m east of Beit Jabr et-Tahtani at the outlet of Wadi Qelt into the Jericho plain; map reference 1907/1396 as printed.
notes: A 'gliding' water mill, perhaps for sugar; linked to the late aqueduct in Wadi Qelt.; A water mill at the outlet of Wadi Qelt, not a cave report; read normally (plan section 7).

site_name: ירושלים: הר ציון (Jerusalem, Mount Zion, old Protestant cemetery)
author: B. Pixner, D. Chen and S. Margalit
location_note: Old Protestant cemetery on Mount Zion; no map reference.
notes: Re-exposure of the gate, earthen road, drain and gate walls with tower 1 found by Bliss and Dickie (1894-1896). Four thresholds, each probably of a different period; no period named. Same campaign as phase-2 ESI02-057-mt-zion (Margalit and Pixner); same feature, not independent.

site_name: ירושלים: בית בד בארמון הנציב (Jerusalem, oil press at Armon ha-Natziv)
author: Y. Gat
location_note: Armon ha-Natziv; no map reference.
notes: The report infers a large farm or agricultural settlement here in the Mishnah and Talmud period; the press installations to be kept in a public garden.

site_name: ירושלים: מאגר מים בצפון תלפיות (Jerusalem, water reservoir in North Talpiyot)
author: A. Kloner and Y. Gat
excavated_or_surveyed: inspected (January 1980); shaft sealed and left in place
location_note: Caspi Street opposite no. 25, North Talpiyot; no map reference.
